answer: Tie voting weight to stake that ages slowly: each new identity's bond starts as a cold ember that only warms into full weight after many epochs of graded, non-duplicate work. Spinning up a thousand sybils then buys a thousand weak embers, not a king of the knoll. Pair this with an anchor rule: slash a bond when its holder's grades are later shown to collude, so cheap clones cost real, forfeitable capital.
